chapter: Dallas childhood, training and early playing
title: Brower's love of Mosaic; hearing it on Symphony Sid's radio show
summary: Brower says Mosaic was one of his first records, and Walton recalls hearing Symphony Sid announce his composition on the radio while driving around Manhattan.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: [inaudible] Mosiac, one of my absolute most favorite recorsings
My little personal moment. That's one of the first three records that I owned.
And last week we talked to Curtis Fuller …
And I just, I got two copies of that. I got a copy that I had from a kid …
… and then later a Japanese import.
But that music and the sound of that music is like, just indelible.

Right. Yeah, I was very happy with that 'cause all of a sudden I'll be riding around Manhattan at night in whatever car I was in, on the radio come Mosaic. The guy, uh, Symphony Sid, the DJ, I guess you would call 'em now – we called 'em that then, a Disc Jockey. He would say, "Yes, that was Mosaic composed by See-Dar Walton. He would pronounce it like "radar." [laughs] I always found that amusing but very exhilarating, you know, ridin' around Manhattan hearing your name on the radio with this music. So that was a good … I've had positive experiences ever since that moment.
